name: Pan-Fried Noodles
steps: Check the noodles are made eggless. Bring 2000 ml water and 5 g salt to a boil. Cook the noodles just until barely tender, following the packet time minus about 1 minute. Drain thoroughly, rinse briefly with cool water and spread on a tray to dry for 5 minutes; damp noodles will steam instead of crisping. Quarter the bok choy, slice mushrooms, cut carrot into matchsticks and trim the snow peas.

Whisk the remaining 200 ml water with soy sauce, vegetarian mushroom sauce, cornstarch and sugar until smooth. Mince the garlic and ginger. Divide the dried noodles into two loose, even nests so each can lie in one layer in the pan.

Heat 18 ml oil in a wide non-stick or well-seasoned pan over medium-high heat. Add one noodle nest, spread it flat and press lightly. Leave undisturbed for 4–5 minutes until the underside forms a golden crust, flip in sections and crisp the other side for 2–3 minutes. Move to a warm serving platter. Repeat with the second nest and another 17 ml oil.

Add the remaining 15 ml oil to the pan. Stir-fry carrot and mushrooms for 2 minutes, then add bok choy stems, snow peas, garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add the leafy bok choy tops and cook another 1 minute; the vegetables should stay bright and slightly crisp.

Stir the sauce again to lift the settled cornstarch, pour it into the hot pan and simmer 1–2 minutes, stirring, until glossy and lightly thickened. Taste; the soy and mushroom sauces provide most of the seasoning. Spoon the vegetables and sauce over the crisp noodle nests only when ready to serve, dividing into four portions so some noodle edges stay crunchy.
tips: Use a mushroom-based vegetarian sauce, not oyster sauce. Thin eggless wheat noodles give the photographed crisp nest; thick soft noodles will not look or eat the same. Sauce the noodles at the table if you want maximum crunch.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
